This document uses data coming from the following article:

- Y. Xu,M.B. Harms,C.S. Green,R.C. Wilson, & S.D. Pollak,  Childhood unpredictability and the development of exploration, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 120 (49) e2303869120, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2303869120 (2023).

We aim to replicate some of the figures and analysis from the paper in order to get some insights for a new project (e.g. required sample size, amount of trials)

# Descriptive statistics 
### Horizon task (**main text table 2**)
```{r}
# Study 1
hr_wide_study1 %>% select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% vtable::st(.)

# Study 2
hr_wide_study2 %>% select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% vtable::st(.)

# t-test
hr_study1 <- hr_wide_study1 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Primary")
hr_study2 <- hr_wide_study2 %>% 
  select(directed_exploration,strategic_exploration,rt_5thchoice,reward_maximization,mean_reward) %>% 
  mutate(study = "Replication")
hr <- rbind(hr_study1,hr_study2)

a <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "directed_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
b <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "strategic_exploration", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
c <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "rt_5thchoice", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
d <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "reward_maximization", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 
e <- rempsyc::nice_t_test(data = hr, response = "mean_reward", group = "study", alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = TRUE) 

bind_rows(a, b, c, d, e) %>% 
  flextable::flextable()

```



```{r}


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom) # Para extraer los coeficientes de los modelos ordenadamente

# 1. Definir la función para extraer los parámetros
get_exploration_params <- function(df) {
  
  # Ajustar el modelo logístico prediciendo la elección de alta información
  # en función de la diferencia de recompensa
  modelo <- glm(chose_high_info_value ~ reward_differential, 
                family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
                data = df)
  
  # Extraer los coeficientes
  coefs <- coef(modelo)
  beta_0 <- coefs["(Intercept)"]
  beta_1 <- coefs["reward_differential"]
  
  # Mapear los coeficientes a los parámetros cognitivos
  # (Se usa el valor absoluto para sigma porque el ruido siempre es positivo)
  sigma <- abs(1 / beta_1)      # Ruido de decisión (Exploración Aleatoria)
  A     <- beta_0 / beta_1      # Bono de Información (Exploración Dirigida)
  
  # Retornar como un data frame de una sola fila
  tibble(
    directed_exploration = A,
    random_exploration = sigma
  )
}

# 2. Aplicar la función a tu tabla por participante y por horizonte
# Nota: Filtramos NAs porque en la condición de información igual [2 2], 
# "chose_high_info_value" no debería estar definido.
parametros_cognitivos <- hr_long_study1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(chose_high_info_value), !is.na(reward_differential)) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
  # group_by(id, horizon) %>%
  group_modify(~ get_exploration_params(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. (Opcional) Pivotar la tabla si necesitas tener los horizontes en columnas 
# separadas para hacer las restas (ej. directed_exploration_H6 - H1)
parametros_anchos <- parametros_cognitivos %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = horizon,
    values_from = c(directed_exploration, random_exploration)
  )

# Ver el resultado
parametros_cognitivos %>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")

hr_wide_study1 %>% 
       select(id, directed_exploration)%>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")

hist(hr_wide_study1$directed_exploration)

```
```{r}

library(tidyverse)

# Adjust if your coding differs (e.g., game_length is 5/10)
df <- hr_long_study1 %>%
  mutate(horizon_f = factor(game_length, levels = c(5, 10),
                            labels = c("short", "long")))

# Sanity check: ~80 games per participant
df %>% count(id) %>% summary()

# % choosing the high-information option, by horizon
de_horizon <- df %>%
  group_by(id, horizon_f) %>%
  summarise(pct_explore = mean(chose_high_info_value, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = horizon_f, values_from = pct_explore,
              names_prefix = "pct_") %>%
  mutate(directed_exploration = pct_long - pct_short)  # horizon-driven increase

# Same, split by reward-information conflict
de_conflict <- df %>%
  group_by(id, horizon_f, conflict) %>%
  summarise(pct_explore = mean(chose_high_info_value, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            .groups = "drop")

# Merge with participant-level variables
subj <- df %>%
  distinct(id, unpredictability, family_income, digit_span, child_anxiety, life_events)

de_subj <- left_join(de_horizon, subj, by = "id")

de_subj %>% 
       select(id, pct_short, pct_long, directed_exploration)%>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")


hr_wide_study1 %>% 
       select(id, directed_exploration,strategic_exploration, short_horizon, long_horizon)%>% 
       filter(id == "1068C")


de_overall <- df %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(n_games = n(),
            directed_exploration = mean(chose_high_info_value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

de_overall %>% filter(id == "1068C")


hr_long_study1%>% filter(id == "1068C")




strategic_subj <- df %>%
  group_by(id, horizon_f) %>%
  summarise(p = mean(chose_high_info_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = horizon_f, values_from = p) %>%
  mutate(strategic_exploration = long - short) %>%
  left_join(df %>% distinct(id, unpredictability, family_income, digit_span), by = "id")

summary(lm(strategic_exploration ~ scale(unpredictability) +
             scale(family_income) + scale(digit_span), data = strategic_subj))


strategic_subj
```
